issues.legal_issue: A second criminal complaint on the same facts is not absolutely barred, but may be entertained only in exceptional circumstances.
material_facts: A first complaint concerning allegedly forged documents and trespass was investigated, and the police concluded that the dispute was civil and that the complainant had executed the acknowledgment.
The Magistrate accepted the police disposal report, and the complainant’s protest petition and complaint were closed; that order was not challenged.
The complainant later filed another complaint on the same allegations, and the High Court set aside the resulting process on the ground that the second complaint was barred.
The Supreme Court held that the second complaint was not completely barred and remitted the matter for the Magistrate to consider afresh whether there was sufficient ground to take cognizance.
issues.conclusion: There is no statutory bar to a second complaint on the same facts, but it may be entertained only in exceptional circumstances. The High Court’s order was set aside, and the Magistrate was directed to consider afresh whether the alleged offences warranted cognizance.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 203 and 204 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, dismissal of a prior complaint does not create an absolute bar to a second complaint on the same facts, though exceptional circumstances are required for its entertainment. Such circumstances include an incomplete record, a misunderstanding of the complaint, a previous order that was manifestly absurd or unjust, or new facts that could not with reasonable diligence have been produced earlier. If the earlier complaint was dismissed without reasons, the Magistrate may take cognizance if sufficient ground for proceeding exists. The Court relied on Pramatha Nath Taluqdar v. Saroj Ranjan Sarkar and Bindeshwari Prasad Singh v. Kali Singh.

rule.if: second_complaint_proceeding and same_allegations_as_prior_complaint and prior_complaint_disposed and (prior_record_incomplete or prior_order_misunderstood_complaint or prior_order_manifestly_absurd_or_unjust or new_facts_unavailable_with_diligence or (prior_dismissal_without_reasons and sufficient_ground_to_proceed))

predicates.second_complaint_proceeding: A complainant initiated a later criminal complaint after an earlier complaint concerning the matter had been disposed of.
predicates.same_allegations_as_prior_complaint: The later complaint alleged substantially the same facts as the earlier complaint.
predicates.prior_complaint_disposed: A court disposed of the earlier complaint.
predicates.prior_record_incomplete: The earlier decision was made on an incomplete record.
predicates.prior_order_misunderstood_complaint: The earlier decision resulted from a misunderstanding of the nature of the complaint.
predicates.prior_order_manifestly_absurd_or_unjust: The earlier decision was manifestly absurd or unjust.
predicates.new_facts_unavailable_with_diligence: The complainant later produced new facts that could not, with reasonable diligence, have been produced in the earlier proceedings.
predicates.prior_dismissal_without_reasons: The earlier complaint was dismissed without reasons being assigned.
predicates.sufficient_ground_to_proceed: The material before the court provided sufficient ground to proceed on the later complaint.
predicates.second_complaint_may_be_entertained: The court may entertain the later complaint.

issues.definition: When a later complaint alleges the same facts as a disposed complaint, it may be entertained if an exceptional circumstance is present, including a reasonless dismissal accompanied by sufficient ground to proceed.
